title: Prove shortest-query and finite-period bounds at all coupled widths
body:
This proof closes arbitrary port coupling as an escape from the shortest-query obstruction. For 4q, 6q and 8q independent fields, the shortest rank-q central-query word needs at least 1, 2 and 3 thin calls, respectively, at every positive q. A block normal form makes the parameterization complete. Ordered free-algebra equations prove the exclusions without assuming that matrix coefficients commute.

The finite-period theorem also holds at every coupled width: a faithful period p >= n-1 forces the formal query identity. A literal native phase and character check therefore excludes the proposed eight-block, nine-full caller with the order-seven stage, including coupling all 104 source ports. Period six, extra queries, initialized work and noncentral native maps remain outside these exclusions. **No new kappa or complete caller is claimed.**

The package also gives the scalar normal form, a short characteristic-not-two identity in four fields, a signed five-call obstruction and a six-call positive control. The alternating query words attain the thin count, but their natural stage endpoint has a nonzero Jordan defect. They do not supply independent Gaussian targets.

[Proof and replay](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/tree/ede796e9d7f04726408bad1cb78e4503b50fb512/research/five-call-projector-rigidity) · [Coupled-width proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ede796e9d7f04726408bad1cb78e4503b50fb512/research/five-call-projector-rigidity/COUPLED.md) · [Validation](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ede796e9d7f04726408bad1cb78e4503b50fb512/research/five-call-projector-rigidity/VALIDATION.md) · [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5593#discussioncomment-19199752)

Validation:

- Registered Python 3.12 replay passes in normal and optimized modes. Each reconstructs 84 scalar and 84 free-associative domains from the chronological products. Literal matrix controls reject commutative word multiplication; block Schur controls check the period extension.
- At proof commit `2e50f9523580a8c1fcb067c779b94a84f52e6eb8`, all 46 package files passed committed-byte and mode checks, official export and input coverage. A read-only Git-free optimized replay passed in 241.036 seconds with an empty PATH. All 47 exported files retained their bytes and modes.
- Direct base ancestry passes. Full-history preflight is unavailable in the shallow checkout. The later validation and timeout metadata retain the checked executable bytes. The timeout is 600 seconds, within the repository cap.

The extension passes [hosted plan and registered replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40812067054) at head `ede796e9d7f04726408bad1cb78e4503b50fb512`. Independent scientific review is pending. No proof-kernel check or selected-frontier replay was run. Discovery files are separate from the proof. DISCOVERY.md discloses and corrects an earlier z-versus-z-1 history-screen error; it did not affect the registered proof. The corrected six-field history exposes two degree-two query directions, not a complete caller.

Base: canonical main `3f0152a32eeebac0df11946dbd50cabe5a7f7839`, priority revision 8. Selected conditional kappa remains .003125804 from PR6030. The original .0034 invoice is only a preliminary screen on its pinned older source. The donor's requested major breakthrough with a large kappa gain remains unmet.

New proofs, replay and discovery: Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Credit Cinna Davis's controller/query lineage and all retained P104, native, helper, caller, compiler and BIT contributors. The related binary split-star certificate, group-word collision results and Dillon/Yiyang border work retain their distinct claims and attribution. Apache-2.0. No merge, closure or selected-frontier change.
